a statement that forms part of the agreement and carries legal force
the principle that a written document cannot be varied by proof of earlier oral statements
a statement of fact made before agreement that induces it without entering it
items.s: Term: a statement that forms part of the agreement and carries legal force. The other options describe Condition, Parol evidence rule, Representation.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Necessaries.
o: a person who has not reached the age of majority, so that agreements with him are usually unenforceable
the purpose to be bound in law, presumed in business dealings but not in family ones
the legal ability of a person to bind himself by an agreement
goods and services suited to the condition in life of a person who cannot support himself
items.s: Necessaries: goods and services suited to the condition in life of a person who cannot support himself. The other options describe Capacity, Intention to create legal relations, Minor.

items.q: “a sum fixed in advance as the agreed compensation for a specified failure” is the definition of
o: Penalty
Liquidated damages
Mitigation of loss
Damages
items.s: Liquidated damages is a sum fixed in advance as the agreed compensation for a specified failure.

items.q: Performance may be defined as
o: the doing of exactly what was undertaken, in the manner agreed
the ending of duties by an unforeseen event that makes performance impossible or pointless
an offer to carry out one's side, which must be refused before complaint
a duty split into parts, each of which can be paid for as it is finished
items.s: Performance: the doing of exactly what was undertaken, in the manner agreed. The other options describe Tender of performance, Divisible obligation, Frustration.

items.q: In this course, Freedom of contract refers to
o: a valid arrangement that a court will not assist because a formality is missing
the side to whom a binding assurance is made
an agreement the law treats as never having existed at all
the principle that parties may fix their own terms without state interference
items.s: Freedom of contract: the principle that parties may fix their own terms without state interference. The other options describe Void contract, Unenforceable agreement, Promisee.

items.q: The correct meaning of Executed consideration is
o: the bar that prevents a person resiling from a clear assurance another relied on
an act done before the promise was made, which therefore cannot support it
the rule that only a party to an agreement may sue upon it
an act already carried out in return for a promise
items.s: Executed consideration: an act already carried out in return for a promise. The other options describe Promissory estoppel, Past consideration, Privity of contract.

items.q: In this course, Silence as acceptance refers to
o: the rule that doing nothing cannot amount to agreement, whatever the proposer says
the principle that a reply sent by mail binds when posted, not when received

a reply making agreement depend on a future event, so acting as a fresh proposal

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Promissory estoppel.

an act done before the promise was made, which therefore cannot support it
the bar that prevents a person resiling from a clear assurance another relied on
something of value given by each side in exchange for the other's undertaking
items.s: Promissory estoppel: the bar that prevents a person resiling from a clear assurance another relied on. The other options describe Past consideration, Sufficiency of consideration, Consideration.

the conveying of agreement to the proposer in a manner that reaches him
the unqualified agreement to every point of a proposal
a reply by telephone or telex that binds only on reaching the proposer
items.s: Communication of acceptance: the conveying of agreement to the proposer in a manner that reaches him. The other options describe Instantaneous communication, Conditional acceptance, Acceptance.
